[DOC002§raft_consensus] Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum error correction codes to protect fragile quantum states from environmental decoherence and gate infidelities. [DOC001§error_correction] The surface code is the leading architecture, arranging physical qubits in a 2D square lattice with alternating

syndrome measurements of star and plaquette stabilizers (X and Z stabilizers). [DOC001§error_correction] Vector clocks are an algorithm for generating a partial ordering of events in a distributed system and detecting causality violations. [DOC002§vector_clocks] Each node maintains an integer vector of size N, incrementing its own index on local events and including its vector clock in transmitted network messages. [DOC002§vector_clocks] Log-Structured Merge Trees (LSM Trees)

are write-optimized storage engines widely used in systems like RocksDB and Cassandra. [DOC003§lsm_trees] Writes are initially appended to a sequential write-ahead log (WAL) and inserted into an in-memory sorted MemTable. [DOC003§lsm_trees] B+Trees organize data hierarchically into fixed-size disk pages (typically 4KB to 16KB). [DOC003§b_trees] Internal nodes store keys and child page pointers, while all records reside in leaf nodes connected as a doubly-linked list.
